text:
nate: Heads-up — we need to spin up a new GPU node pool in asia-south1 for compact-infer fastpath. Goal: sustain ~1.2k qps spikey traffic, p90 latency target ~120ms. Can someone sanity-check size + autoscaler + taint/backfill plan?

maria: do we have a target instance SKU? preemptible preferred? :thinking_face:

nate: prefer A10G preemptible for cost. Plan is a primary preemptible pool + reserved H100 pool as fallback for steady traffic if preemptibles get churned. Also need to ensure egress IPs for customer-A workload (they require static NAT).

sachin: quick quota check — cloud console shows ~160 GPUs free in asia-south1 under current quota (across SKUs). If we target ~24 A10G nodes with 4 GPUs each that's ~96 GPUs, seems ok but we should request headroom.

olivia: we only have 3 NAT IPs left in that region. If inference pods need dedicated egress per-customer, we must request additional egress IPs or route through shared egress for now.

kai: suggested autoscaler config (sketch):
```yaml
nodePool:
  name: infer-apse1-a10g-preempt
  machineType: a10g-standard-32
  gpusPerNode: "4"
  autoscaling:
    minNodes: 4
    maxNodes: 40
    targetUtilization: 0.65
  taints:
    - key: redwood/gpu
      value: inference
      effect: NoSchedule
  labels:
    workload: compact-infer
```
Add podPriority + podDisruptionBudget so canary traffic survives preemptions.

maria: for the fallback pool we should set nodeAffinity/taints so traffic only lands there when preemptible capacity < threshold. Cluster-autoscaler supports multiple node pools — we can implement a routing policy via our smart router: route to preemptible first, if latency degrades route to reserved.

nate: good. How do we detect "preemptible capacity < threshold" automatically?

kai: two signals: cluster-autoscaler scale failures + queue build-up in our routing metrics. We can run a short circuit: if tail latency > 200ms for 3m AND preemptible count < 25%, flip routing weight. We'll add an alert.

sachin: note on quotas: if you plan for A10G specifically, quota requests are SKU-specific in the console. I can open a ticket requesting +200 A10G GPUs and +10 NAT IPs. That should be enough headroom for next month.

olivia: networking note — subnet IP exhaustion in that VPC is possible with 40+ nodes + burst. Can we use smaller pod CIDRs or use alias IP ranges? Also need to set up NAT auto-provisioning.

nate: good catch. Kai, please include node ip/egress checklist in preflight.

kai: will do. Also recommending kubelet args to accelerate eviction handling for preemptions:
```
--eviction-hard=memory.available<200Mi,nodefs.available<10%
--eviction-soft=nodefs.available<15%:30s
--pod-eviction-timeout=2m
```
This reduces pod bounce on spot churn.

maria: add a priorityClass for inference-canary so the canary pods survive longer than background batch jobs. Example: `kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: inference-canary
value: 200000
globalDefault: false
description: "Priority for live inference canaries"
EOF`

infra-bot: Reminder: please file quota request at https://console.cloud/quotas and include region=asia-south1, SKUs=[A10G, H100], NAT_IPs=10. Ticket template: infra/quotas/new.

nate: action items I got: @sachin open quota ticket for GPUs + NAT IPs; @kai prepare preflight nodepool config + ip/egress checklist + cluster-autoscaler tuning; @maria add priorityClass + PDB; olivia to verify subnet CIDR headroom. I'll do a canary launch with 4 nodes (preemptible) after quotas submitted. :thumbsup:

maria: tiny perf-safety ask — set `targetUtilization` conservative at 0.6 for first week so we don't starve latency-sensitive slots on burst.

nate: ack. I'll set targetUtilization=0.6 for canary then 0.65 for full rollout.

sachin: ticket opened: QC-3245, requested +220 A10G, +40 H100 reserved fallback, +10 NAT IPs. ETA for approval ~24-72h.

nate: perfect. we'll wait on quota then create infra PR. Thanks all.

kai: posting preflight checklist in #eng-infra/preflight when ready (will include k8s manifest snippets, CA flags, and egress playbook).

nate: closing thread — will update when quotas land.
